text:
The plate holds two corn-on-the-cob pieces, each about 4 cm long, plus one loose kernel. They look like short cross-sections of a cob, about 5-6 cm in diameter.

Each piece is roughly 5 cm across and 3-4 cm long, so about 60-70 g of kernels plus cob. Two pieces come to about 130-150 g, and I'll use 140 g in total.

Corn on the cob runs about 0.9-1.0 kcal/g for the kernels, but the cob itself is heavy and adds little. Counting the cob, I estimate about 0.7 kcal/g, which gives about 100 kcal.

```json
{"kcal": 100, "mass_g": 140}
```
